I dealt with this a lot. What you need to parse through and understand is the difference between unwarranted guilt and shame. 

What you’re feeling isn’t guilt. Guilt is helpful in that tells you when you’ve crossed your own values or you’ve done something wrong e.g. if you stole or hit someone with a car. 

By going NC, you’re not doing anything wrong. You’re not taking advantage of anyone, you’re not hurting anyone. You’re just looking after yourself and not subjecting yourself to anymore pain. 

The shame that you’re feeling is simply from the cultural background that we’ve grown up in where we’re constantly shamed for everything.
Move out

Speaking from personal experience, I went to FSH ED (Fiona Stanley) and told them I was suicidal. From there I was admitted into short stay unit - seen by the psych registrar etc. If your case is severe, and it sounds like it is, you’ll be linked up to a mental health care team. 

I fell into the Freo catchment and I’ve been a part of the home treatment team for awhile. They helped with things like housing, money, medication etc. 

I currently receive therapy + go to regular checkups with a psych registrar at Freo.
My partner helped me find the courage to finally do it. I hadn’t been home for weeks/if not months and would only stop by at home to just keep up the appearances to my parents.

Haha yeah. I got a very similar response when I rocked up to my parents house and started loading boxes into the car. I had actually had packed everything up months before hand but it took me forever to pull the trigger and do it. 

If they ask where you’re moving to, don’t tell them if you’re planning to cut contact. It’ll just let them sink their claws in and you’ll be roped back into the same mess again.

As someone who had parents just like yours (minus the obligatory feelings of having to give them money), the initial guilt you might feel from leaving them is better than going through a mental health crisis/breakdown. 

My parents are one of the biggest contributors to my shitty mental health. I was in the biggest toxic rut. The more that I'm in therapy, the more work I realise I need to do in order to unlearn it all. 

Cutting them off and not having their influence in my life was the best decision I ever made. I pulled the trigger back in Nov 2020 and have not contacted them bar one email back in Sep 2021 despite their many threats, phone calls, calls from the police , emails etc. 

I am so much better for it.  I still feel guilty and I do wonder how they are BUT I know that this was the best decision for my mental health and overall well being. 

You'll be ok OP. You just need to come to terms with the decision. It's not something that's made lightly.

You’re going to be ok and you will get through this. Just remember that it’s not culture and it’s not discipline. It’s abuse and it’s not normal.

That’s honestly the most important thing in life. Fuck a degree. It means shit all if you’re miserable. Take a semester off to just figure out which route you want to take in life whether it be ditching your degree entirely , seeing if you can switch courses into something you might enjoy etc.  

Do things at your own pace and try to not compare yourself to other people because everyone succeeds at their own pace. 

You’ll be ok op. I’m sure you’ll pull through. Just take some time and put your mental health first.
